chapter_info.text:
Name

The 1st surah of the Qur’an, al-Fatiha (“The Opening”), is named because it opens the Book. It is also known by many other names due to its excellence and central importance. Among its names are: The Opener, The Mother of the Book, The Seven Oft-Recited Verses, The Praise, The Supplication, The Healer, The Light, The Foundation, and others.

Period of Revelation

As said above al-Fatiha is the 5th surah in chronological order, revealed after Surah al-Muddaththir. There are three opinions regarding its revelation: (1) it is Meccan, (2) it is Medinan, or (3) it was revealed twice—once in Mecca and once in Medina. The majority opinion holds that it belongs to the Meccan period.

This surah consists of seven verses, and it holds a unique status as it is recited repeatedly in daily prayers.

Theme

Surah al-Fatiha encapsulates the fundamental themes of faith. It presents the relationship between the Creator and creation, affirms Allah’s absolute authority in this world and the Hereafter, and highlights the constant dependence of human beings upon Him for guidance and assistance.

It describes Allah as the Lord and Sustainer of all worlds, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, and the Master of the Day of Judgment.

The surah teaches the proper manners of worship—sincerity, humility, devotion, and obedience. It emphasizes that Allah alone is worthy of worship and that help should be sought only from Him.

It further instructs believers to seek guidance to the straight path—the path of those who are blessed, not of those who incur wrath or go astray. This reflects the mindset of a sincere seeker of truth.

Al-Fatiha also represents a dialogue between the servant and Allah. As mentioned in hadith, Allah responds to each verse recited by the servant in prayer, affirming praise, devotion, and supplication, and granting what is asked.

Due to its عظيمة (great significance), the Prophet ﷺ described it as a unique surah unmatched in previous scriptures, and as the “Seven Oft-Repeated Verses” given to his الأمة.
